chief_complaint: Chronic pain management with multiple opioid analgesics in the setting of metabolic syndrome and uncontrolled hypertension
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 49-year-old Hispanic white male with a long-standing history of type 2 diabetes (diagnosed 1999), essential hypertension (diagnosed 1999) and metabolic syndrome. Obesity (BMI >30) was documented in 2016 and hypertriglyceridemia since 2000. Chronic neck pain and generalized chronic pain have been present since 2014, leading to the prescription of several opioid-containing analgesics (codeine, oxycodone, hydrocodone, tramadol) and occasional NSAID use. Stress was noted beginning in 2017. Anemia has been recorded since 1999 and is being treated with oral iron. The most recent laboratory data show a hemoglobin A1c of 6.1% (prediabetic range) but no recent blood pressure, lipid panel, or renal function values are available. The latest acute issue is otitis media diagnosed on 2020-10-19. The patient works full‑time, is a refugee since 2010, and has higher education. He has had limited outpatient encounters (2) and primarily wellness visits, suggesting possible gaps in routine chronic disease monitoring.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include recurrent gingivitis (most recent resolution 2019-12-19), multiple medication review reminders (2016-2019), acute viral pharyngitis (resolved 2019-08-11), and acute infective cystitis (resolved 2018-10-16). These reflect intermittent oral health issues and prior urinary tract infection.
